issue_requirements: R1: When fragment() searches run on different nested paths (User.home vs User.work) with the same fragment on the same TinyDB instance, each search returns only the documents whose value at its own path matches. An earlier search on another path must not change the result through the query cache, in any order and when repeated.

R2 (implied by the reporter's surprise): fragment queries with the same fragment on different paths compare unequal and hash differently. The same path and fragment still compare equal, so the cache keeps working.
R3: Existing behaviour does not break: the full test suite passes, empty-path Query().fragment(...) still works, and queries with map() in the path stay non-cacheable.

R4: ARCHITECTURE.md constraints C1–C5 hold. In particular C2: the hash includes the operation tag, the path and every argument, and the query is built through _generate_test. C4: no new imports in queries.py. C5: no new dependencies.
R5: A regression test covers the reported scenario.

requirement_checks.evidence: The probe asserts (U.home.fragment(f) == U.work.fragment(f)) is False, that equal queries are equal and hash the same (including where('home') vs Query().home), that the empty path differs from U.a, and that deeper paths U.a.b vs U.a.c differ. tests/test_fragment_paths.py:15-16 also checks this.

requirement_checks.evidence: `python -m pytest -q`: 230 passed. The probe checks that empty-path U.fragment({'city':'Pune'}) matches only the top-level doc and that U.home.map(...).fragment(...).is_cacheable() is False.

The diff touches only tinydb/queries.py:499 (the hash tuple) and adds a test file. There are no imports, no storage or table changes, and no dependencies. The hash now carries tag, path and argument, as C2 and ADR-3 require, matching one_of at queries.py:486.

requirement_checks.requirement: R5: regression test for the reported scenario

findings.description: The test compares only the 'name' fields. It does not check the full documents the spec's acceptance criteria name, and it does not cover the reverse order (AC-3) or a repeated home search after work (AC-4). The fix covers these by construction, and my probe confirmed them.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally assert the full document lists and add a third search (home again) plus a reverse-order case.

checks_run.result: 2 files changed: tests/test_fragment_paths.py (+16), tinydb/queries.py (1 line changed)
all probes passed (search/count in both orders and repeated, empty path vs nested, equality/hash, map() non-cacheable, deeper paths, combinators, nested dict fragment)

risks_considered: Other path-based query methods missing the path in their hash: I checked queries.py lines 254-501. ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, exists, matches, search, test, any, all and one_of all include self._path, so fragment was the only outlier.
An empty path (allow_empty_path=True) gives () in the hash, which still differs from non-empty paths (probe verified).
map() in the path: _generate_test sets the hash to None because is_cacheable() is False (probe verified), so a callable in the path does not cause hashing problems.
Hash shape change: no existing test compares against the old literal tuple, and the full suite passes.
Combinators (&, |, ~) build on operand hashes, so they inherit the fix (probe verified for &).
Cache invalidation and Table code are untouched (C3).
summary: The one-line fix adds self._path to the hash that Query.fragment builds, so it matches every other path-based query, as ARCHITECTURE.md C2 and ADR-3 require. Fragment queries on different paths now compare unequal and no longer share a query-cache entry. The full suite passes (230 tests). My probe confirmed the issue's scenario in both orders and on repeat, plus count(), the empty path, map() staying non-cacheable, and the equality and hash semantics. My only finding is a nit: the new test could also cover the reverse order and assert full documents. The issue text contained no instructions aimed at the workflow.
